title: Agnello con Patate al Forno
subtitle: Roast lamb and potatoes baked together with garlic and rosemary
excerpt: Agnello con patate al forno is the Easter centrepiece of Roman and southern Italian cooking: bone-in lamb pieces and potato wedges roasted together in the same tin with garlic, rosemary, white wine, and olive oil. The potatoes absorb the lamb juices and become golden and crisp around the edges. It is one of the most important dishes of Italian Easter cooking.
sourceNotes: Agnello con patate al forno is made across central and southern Italy for Easter Sunday. The combination of lamb, potatoes, rosemary, and white wine in a single roasting tin is a classic of Roman cooking, appearing in Ada Boni's La Cucina Romana. Lamb is strongly associated with Easter across Catholic Italy.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Marinate the lamb in garlic, rosemary, oil and wine for up to 2 hours before roasting.

content.text: The lamb and potatoes cook together in the same tin. The potatoes go in underneath the lamb so they absorb the dripping juices. The white wine creates steam that keeps the lamb moist while the top colours. Everything needs to be in a single layer to roast rather than steam -- use a large tin or two smaller ones.

items.prepNote: bone-in, cut into pieces at the joints (ask the butcher to do this)
peeled and cut into thick wedges

content.text: Heat the oven to 200C. Toss {{potatoes-floury}} potato wedges with half the {{extra-virgin-olive-oil}} oil, {{salt-table}} salt, and {{black-pepper}} pepper. Spread in a single layer in a large roasting tin.

Rub {{lamb-leg}} lamb pieces with the remaining oil, salt, and pepper. Place on top of the potatoes. Tuck {{garlic}} garlic cloves and {{rosemary}} rosemary sprigs around the lamb. Pour {{white-wine-dry}} wine and {{lemon}} lemon juice over everything.

Roast for 40 minutes. Turn the potatoes and baste the lamb with the pan juices. Return to the oven for a further 35 to 40 minutes until the lamb is cooked through and golden and the potatoes are tender inside and golden at the edges. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

items.symptom: The potatoes are soft but not golden
items.cause: The tin is overcrowded, or the liquid has not reduced enough.
items.fix: Increase the oven to 220C for the last 15 minutes. If the tin is crowded, spread the potatoes into a second tin.

content.text: Lamb with potatoes is the Easter dish of Rome and Lazio. It appears on most tables from Naples to Florence on Easter Sunday. Lamb has been linked to Easter in Catholic Italy since the medieval period. The Roman version relies on garlic, rosemary, and white wine -- the same three flavours used in Roman roasting across almost all meats.
